title: A monthly class calendar that knows the special-class rotation
need: Lower School classrooms wanted a one-page monthly calendar that shows which special class each day falls on.
built: A calendar builder with the Lausanne rotation built in. Add your name, classes, birthdays and events, then choose color or black and white.

title: A weekly agenda you write once and paste into Toddle
need: Teachers were retyping the same class plans into Toddle posts, with days, periods and times to look up each week.
built: The Lausanne Weekly Agenda: pick your division and periods, write each class meeting once, and the rotation days and times fill in. Mark days a class does not meet, then copy the finished text for a Toddle post.

title: Name sheets that teach letters on the Chromebook keyboard
need: Young students needed practice finding the letters of their own name on a Chromebook keyboard.
built: A generator that makes one page per student: the name to trace, a keyboard to color in key by key, and a line for the Chromebook number.

title: A Little Lynx Computer Lab for Senior Kindergarten
need: Senior Kindergarten students had never used a Chromebook, and teachers wanted a ready plan.
built: A student site with a card for each of the six weeks, from Hello, Chromebook! to Share and Celebrate!, each with short activities students play through. A link to the teacher guide sits underneath.

title: A picture-based research library for first graders
need: First graders researching animals and plants needed safe, readable sources they could cite.
built: Picture cards by animal, plant and habitat with read-aloud buttons, vocabulary, credited photos, video and Epic book links, and copy-ready citations.

title: A "what color day is it?" schedule for students
need: Students kept losing track of which classes fall on which day of the rotating color schedule.
built: Pick a color day to see classes in order with teachers and rooms, or view the whole week. Students can edit it and save a picture of their schedule.

title: A pretend grocery store for reading nutrition labels
need: A 7th grade nutrition project needed realistic food labels to read, without using real brands or real people's data.
built: Lynx Market, a made-up grocery store where students browse aisles, flip packages to read their Nutrition Facts labels, and use meal logs, a shopping cart and a Maya's Week section. Teachers can print label cards.

title: A Flex Period sign-up system built around teacher feedback
need: Microsoft Bookings made Flex sign-ups clunky: teachers could not see their roster and it did not fit advisories.
built: Flex Bookings, a site where teachers see each teacher's open spots by day and book students in. It includes My bookings, My roster, My advisees, sign-ups and admin controls, and it uses your Lausanne Microsoft sign-in.

title: Printable grade detail pages from a Toddle export
need: Toddle does not print a per-student grade page the way Veracross used to.
built: Drop in a Toddle gradebook export, pick students, and print or save a page for each one. Everything runs in your browser.

title: A one-page guide to Toddle notification settings for families
need: Families were getting more Toddle email than they wanted and did not know where to change it.
built: A branded handout with numbered steps for the web and the mobile app, screenshots, and an email troubleshooting note.

title: MYP rubric level to percentage and letter grade
need: Teachers entering MYP summative grades in Toddle needed a quick conversion chart.
built: A one-page chart that maps each rubric level, 8 down to 0, to a percentage and a letter grade.

title: An eight-week mock trial pre-season plan
need: Students needed to learn how a trial works before the new case was released, so practice time could go to strategy.
built: Sixteen practices in four phases, each with a warm-up, skill block, application and debrief, plus a drill bank and resources.
